venue.title: A Window on Canton, from seat to payout
venue.subtitle: Your seat accepts a firm quote; ops keeps the clock and prints moving; the Daml contracts decide and pay.
venue.note: This path runs end to end on a local Canton sandbox with demo credits; nothing is on DevNet or a hosted URL yet. Each Window's price source is named on its Series policy and on every receipt.

nodes.title: Seat key
nodes.subtitle: ed25519, browser or Keychain
nodes.detail: Take a seat makes a signing key the page cannot export (on the iPhone, in the Keychain for this device only), and the venue leases a Canton party to it. The key proves each request; ops never holds it.
nodes.authority: Proves which lease is asking. It never names a party itself.

nodes.title: Web ticket
nodes.subtitle: Window, side, stake, quote
nodes.detail: The ticket reads the venue's price ladder and asks for a firm quote for one side at your stake. It shows the cost, fee included, before you accept; the quote holds for about 20 seconds.
nodes.authority: Displays and prepares a call. A quote on screen is not a fill.

nodes.title: Seat routes
nodes.subtitle: Party from the lease
nodes.detail: The web's seat and ledger routes check the seat's proof, look up its current lease and submit as that lease's party only, through packages/markets and the JSON Ledger API v2 client.
nodes.authority: On a shared participant this code decides which party acts; the no-party-from-request invariant guards it.

nodes.title: Quote_Accept
nodes.subtitle: abu-pm-main on the participant
nodes.detail: Accepting spends your VenueCash and creates two Legs: yours and the venue's opposite one. Your Leg is signed by the venue and your party, so only the two of you can see it.
nodes.authority: The Daml checks price, expiry, cash and ownership. The venue cannot accept a quote for you.

nodes.title: Window roller
nodes.subtitle: Series_OpenWindow
nodes.detail: Opens each Window on its Series' cadence (a Monday Gap by span, an event by question) under the Series' current price-policy version.
nodes.authority: Can list Windows. It cannot resolve or pay.

nodes.title: Three oracle parties
nodes.subtitle: PriceQuote at each boundary
nodes.detail: Coinbase, Kraken and Bitstamp 1-minute closes for crypto; for every other lane each oracle party reads the named source itself. The raw response is archived and its sha-256 goes on the quote.
nodes.authority: Each oracle signs only its own quotes.

nodes.title: Resolver
nodes.subtitle: Terms_Resolve or Terms_Void
nodes.detail: Records the open, then resolves the close from at least 2 of 3 quotes whose spread is within 1% of their median, or voids with a named reason. The Resolution is signed by the resolver and the venue.
nodes.authority: Needs the oracle quorum; the venue cannot resolve alone. A Window resolves or voids exactly once.

nodes.title: Settler
nodes.subtitle: Desk_SettleBatch
nodes.detail: Pays each resolved Window's legs to their owners' cash in batches; a void returns stake plus fee. The owner signs nothing.
nodes.authority: Pays only by the recorded Resolution. From the refund time the venue cannot settle and the owner can take a stale refund.

nodes.title: Venue's updates
nodes.subtitle: /v2/updates as the venue
nodes.detail: The ledger's transactions as the venue sees them, each with its update id.
nodes.authority: The venue sees its own contracts and the legs it is counterparty to, nothing else.

nodes.title: Projector
nodes.subtitle: Updates into Postgres
nodes.detail: Follows the stream and writes Windows, prints, quotes, fills and resolutions into tables. verify-projection compares them with the ledger, and a rebuild from offset 0 must equal the live tables.
nodes.authority: Read-only on the ledger. It cannot change a result.

nodes.title: Seat reads
nodes.subtitle: Your party, your lease
nodes.detail: Your cash, legs and receipts are read as your leased party, from the offset your lease began, so a recycled party never shows a previous visitor's history.
nodes.authority: Bound to the current lease, never to the party alone.

nodes.title: Portfolio and Proof
nodes.subtitle: Receipts, update ids
nodes.detail: Portfolio shows positions and receipts. /proof shows each Window's prints, oracles and resolution timeline, and Re-verify re-hashes the archived payloads and re-reads the exchange candles.
nodes.authority: A page is a view of ledger evidence; the update id is the receipt.

desk.title: The desk on Canton
desk.subtitle: The owner sets the mandate; the operator chooses only when; the ledger checks every trade.
desk.note: A practice desk is a paper ledger kept by the runner. A live DeskMandate has been opened, funded, paused, resumed and checkpointed on a local Canton sandbox; it has not traded there yet, because no model key was set. Demo credits only.

nodes.title: Owner seat
nodes.subtitle: Names, limits, money
nodes.detail: The owner picks the pre-IPO names (their 60-minute Series), the premium ceiling and the caps, and funds the desk from the seat's demo credits.
nodes.authority: Only the owner changes limits, deposits, withdraws or closes.

nodes.title: Desk studio
nodes.subtitle: Draft, practice, go live
nodes.detail: The browser keeps the draft; a signed message starts a paper practice desk. Going live needs six hourly practice checks.
nodes.authority: Practice moves no money.

nodes.title: DeskOffer_Open
nodes.subtitle: Creates the DeskMandate
nodes.detail: The venue's standing DeskOffer lets the owner open a DeskMandate from their own cash: allowlist, premium ceiling, attestors, mode, and an embedded AgentGrant with its caps.
nodes.authority: Signed by the owner and the venue; the operator only observes it.

nodes.title: Owner choices
nodes.subtitle: Unpause, withdraw, close
nodes.detail: Unpause, set limits, set the allowlist, change or revoke the operator, deposit, withdraw and close are the owner's choices on the mandate.
nodes.authority: The operator may pause the desk but never unpause it, change a limit or withdraw.

nodes.title: DeskMarks
nodes.subtitle: Oracle marks, 2 of 3
nodes.detail: The oracle parties post DeskMark contracts at a Window's fair Up price. The reference is the lower median of at least two marks, none older than 15 minutes.
nodes.authority: An attestor learns its mark was read, not by whom or for how much.

nodes.title: Desk runner
nodes.subtitle: Prices, timing, a decision
nodes.detail: The runner reads the PreStocks prices and the venue's quotes at the owner's size, asks a model one bounded timing question, and writes a desk.v1 record with a decision hash.
nodes.authority: Proposes only. It cannot change limits or withdraw.

nodes.title: Mandate_Trade
nodes.subtitle: Up lots on an allowed name
nodes.detail: The operator buys one of the owner's firm venue quotes on an allowed Series: at most the premium ceiling above the attested reference, then every grant cap (per trade, per day, budget, open positions) inside Grant_AcceptQuote.
nodes.authority: The ledger refuses a trade that breaks any limit.

nodes.title: Mandate_Sell
nodes.subtitle: Only what the desk bought
nodes.detail: A venue buy-back quote on one of the owner's legs the desk bought, at no less than 92% of the attested value; the proceeds return to the desk's budget.
nodes.authority: Cannot sell the owner's other positions.

nodes.title: Owner's legs
nodes.subtitle: Ordinary positions
nodes.detail: A bought lot is an ordinary Leg of the owner's party; the mandate counts it in its holdings until the Window's refund time.
nodes.authority: It settles like any call: the settler pays the owner's seat.

nodes.title: DeskDecision
nodes.subtitle: Hash chain, every action
nodes.detail: Every trade, sale or checkpoint leaves a DeskDecision and advances head(n) = sha256(head(n−1) : n : decisionHash). The operator must name the head it builds on.
nodes.authority: A forked or replayed record is refused.

nodes.title: Daily checkpoint
nodes.subtitle: Even when nothing trades
nodes.detail: Mandate_Checkpoint seals a no-action decision into the same chain; the runner's daily pass runs at 00:05 UTC.
nodes.authority: Allowed while the desk is paused.

nodes.title: Desk cockpit
nodes.subtitle: Value, activity, rules
nodes.detail: The pages read the mandate, its holdings, decisions and record, and label practice separately from live.
nodes.authority: A paper balance is not seat cash.

prints.title: Where a Canton print comes from
prints.subtitle: Three oracle parties read the named source; the resolver needs two that agree.
prints.note: Every lane settles on the same PriceQuote path. Crypto reads three exchanges; stocks read RedStone (QQQ and VOO: Alpaca's last IEX trade); xStocks read Jupiter Price v3, the median of three samples; pre-IPO names and baskets read the PreStocks catalogue. Pyth is not used: there is no entitled key.

nodes.title: Three exchanges
nodes.subtitle: Coinbase, Kraken, Bitstamp
nodes.detail: Each oracle party reads its own exchange's 1-minute candle; the close of the candle ending at the boundary is its price.
nodes.authority: One exchange per oracle party; a candle that is not final in time is not posted.

nodes.title: Oracle feeders
nodes.subtitle: Post at T + 10 s
nodes.detail: At each minute boundary each feeder posts a PriceQuote for every symbol, command id print:<oracle>:<T>. The raw response is archived byte for byte.
nodes.authority: Each feeder signs as its own oracle party only.

nodes.title: PriceQuote
nodes.subtitle: Signed by one oracle
nodes.detail: Symbol, bar, price and the sha-256 of the raw payload, seen by the venue and the resolver.
nodes.authority: A quote alone decides nothing.

nodes.title: Quorum check
nodes.subtitle: 2 of 3, spread within 1%
nodes.detail: The resolver counts distinct valid quotes admitted for the boundary and takes their median. A spread over 1% of the median voids the Window as a source disagreement.
nodes.authority: Fewer than two quotes cannot resolve; the Window voids instead.

nodes.title: Original source
nodes.subtitle: Named on the Series policy
nodes.detail: Stocks read RedStone (QQQ and VOO: Alpaca's last IEX trade), xStocks read Jupiter Price v3 (the median of three samples), and pre-IPO names and baskets read the PreStocks catalogue. The policy text, such as attested:redstone:TSLA, names it.
nodes.authority: The source is not a Canton party; the oracle parties attest what they read.

nodes.title: Lane feeders
nodes.subtitle: Each oracle reads it itself
nodes.detail: Only for the boundaries a listed Window needs, each oracle party reads the source inside its timing window and posts its own quote. A basket print is an equal-weight index in points from one catalogue read of every member.
nodes.authority: A read that misses its window is not posted, and the Window voids on the missing print.

nodes.title: Attested PriceQuote
nodes.subtitle: Same contract, same rules
nodes.detail: Attested prints are the same PriceQuote with the same quorum and 1% rule as crypto, each carrying its payload hash.
nodes.authority: One path for every lane: two agreeing oracle quotes, or a void.

nodes.title: Source on the receipt
nodes.subtitle: Every receipt names it
nodes.detail: The proof page and receipts read the policy text and name the source: RedStone, Alpaca (last IEX trade), Jupiter Price v3 (median of three samples), PreStocks or a committee attestation.
nodes.authority: A receipt never presents an attested read as an independent oracle.

nodes.title: Opening print
nodes.subtitle: Terms_RecordOpen
nodes.detail: The resolver records the median of the admitted open quotes as the OpenPrint, consuming the Window's state.
nodes.authority: Signed by the resolver and the venue.

nodes.title: Closing print
nodes.subtitle: Admitted until its deadline
nodes.detail: Close quotes count only inside the source's admission window after expiry. A slot with no quorum by its deadline voids.
nodes.authority: A late quote does not count.

nodes.title: Resolution
nodes.subtitle: Up, Down or Void, once
nodes.detail: Terms_Resolve or Terms_Void consumes the OpenPrint, so a Window resolves or voids exactly once. A close equal to the open pays Up.
nodes.authority: Signed by the resolver and the venue; the venue alone cannot create it.

nodes.title: Proof page
nodes.subtitle: Prints, hashes, re-verify
nodes.detail: /proof/<market> shows each oracle's quote, the median, the archive hash and the resolution timeline; Re-verify re-hashes the archive and re-reads the exchange candles.
nodes.authority: A readable trail; the Resolution's update id is the receipt.
